15. By the health of Pharao. † Ioſeph in ſwearing by Pharaos health , hono-
red God, the geuer and conſeruer of health, life, power, dignitie and al that
was in Pharao. wherby we fee that this maner of ſwearing was lawful. As now
likewiſe Chriſtians lawfully ſweare not only by God, but alſo by his creatures,
ſaying : As God ſhal helpe them, & his holie Goſpels: ſo it be with due circum-
ſtances, and requiſite conditions, namely with thoſe which the Prophet Hie-
Hier. 4. remie mentione th, in truth, in iudgem ent, and in iuſtice : not ſalfe, raſh, nor of an
vniuſt thing : nor in frequent and cōmon talke (a moſt bad cuſtome) for ſo
Mat. 5. thou muſt neirher ſweare by God himſelf, nor (as our ſauiour teacheth) by
heauen, nor by the earth, nor by Hieruſalem, nor by thy head, nor anie thing
els: fignifying that in ſome caſe, and due manet we may ſweare by any of theſe.
And in this particular Ioſeph did rather name Pharao in his oath then God, as
wel to conceale himſelf as yet from his brethren, as to ſtrike more terrour in
their hartes, by naming his maſter tht Ring, in whom he had more intereſt
then thcy.
